mainTopic: A יבמה who says the ייבום never happened: חליצה, גט, and the rival wife. Then whether a vow against all Jews also covers the יבם.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an answer from the previous page: in the first thirty days the יבם may simply be too shy with the יבמה, so her claim that nothing happened is believable. The גמרא asks why the court forces חליצה instead of forcing him to finish the ייבום. רב answers that he already gave her a גט. A ברייתא seems to challenge רב. רבי אמי and רב אשי each give a way to answer it. In a real case, רבא first rules that חליצה alone is enough. When רב שרביא quotes the ברייתא requiring a גט and חליצה, רבא accepts it. רב נחמן then rules that this woman's claim does not make her rival wife (צרה) forbidden. Next the גמרא turns to the woman who vows against her יבם. It quotes a משנה from נדרים about three claims that once let a wife leave with her כתובה, until the חכמים tightened the rules. That leads to a question: does the vow 'I am withdrawn from the Jews' also cover the יבם? רב says no, שמואל says yes, and אביי begins a proof for רב that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He may still be shy with her
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an answer from the previous page: within the first thirty days a man may be too embarrassed to be with his new wife, so we believe her claim that nothing happened.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of an answer that started on the previous page. It explains why, within thirty days, we do not assume the יבם has already lived with the יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After thirty days we assume a husband has already been with his wife. In the first thirty days, though, he might still feel shy with her, so it is quite possible nothing has happened yet. That is why her claim of 'לא נבעלתי' is taken seriously in that window.

keyTerms.meaning: he is embarrassed / shy
with her, from her

phrases.english: He is embarrassed with her.
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from the previous page: in the first thirty days he may be too shy to be with her yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends an answer begun on the previous page about the thirty-day difference in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a fact about how people behave
steps.terutzMaskana: Within thirty days it is believable that he has not yet been with her, because he may be shy.

steps.title: Why force חליצה instead of forcing ייבום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the court forces him to do חליצה. It could just as easily force him to complete the ייבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before we force him to perform חליצה, let us force him to perform ייבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling in the משנה that the court forces the יבם to do חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem is only that he has not yet lived with her, the court can force him to finish the ייבום. That would fulfill the main מצוה. Choosing חליצה looks like the less sensible option.

keyTerms.meaning: we (the court) force
the ceremony that releases a יבמה without ייבום
to perform ייבום (levirate marriage)

phrases.english: Rather than forcing him to perform חליצה,
let us force him to perform ייבום!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁכּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ לַחְלוֹץ נִיכְפֶּנּוּ לְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why her claim is believed to why the remedy is חליצה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the court forces חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he simply has not yet lived with her, forcing ייבום is the more natural fix.

steps.title: רב: she already holds a גט from him
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the משנה is talking about a case where the יבם already gave her a גט, so ייבום is no longer an option.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is a case where her גט is coming out from under her hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by narrowing the case of the משנה. The יבם has already divorced her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he has given her a גט, he cannot go back and do ייבום with her. If he never actually lived with her, the גט alone does not fully release her, so she still needs חליצה. Forcing חליצה is therefore the only option left.

keyTerms.meaning: her bill of divorce
is in her possession (literally, comes out from under her hand)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גט makes חליצה unnecessary. She says the ייבום never happened, so the גט by itself does not release her from the יבם.

phrases.english: רב said:
When her גט is already in her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בְּשֶׁגִּיטָּהּ יוֹצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדָהּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a regular case where ייבום could still be forced.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a case where he already gave her a גט, so only חליצה is possible.

steps.title: A ברייתא with the same thirty-day rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same rulings as the משנה. Within thirty days the court forces חליצה, and after thirty days it only asks for it. This sets up the challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: A יבמה who said within thirty days 'I did not have relations,' whether he says 'I did' or 'I did not,' they force him to do חליצה. After thirty days, they ask him to do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a challenge to רב by quoting a ברייתא. This first part repeats the rules of the משנה and prepares the ground for the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within thirty days her claim wins even if he says he did live with her, so the court forces חליצה. After thirty days we assume they were together, so the court can only ask him. The real attack comes from how the ברייתא continues.

keyTerms.meaning: they objected (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
widow waiting for ייבום or חליצה
I had relations
we request (not force)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A יבמה who said within thirty days
'I did not have relations with him' —
whether he says 'I had relations with her,'
or whether he says 'I did not have relations with her,'
they force him to perform חליצה for her.
After thirty days —
they ask him to perform חליצה for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי יְבָמָה שֶׁאָמְרָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רב's answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the case involves a woman who already has a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא's later lines will show that its case has no גט yet.

steps.title: The ברייתא requires a גט, so she has none yet
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to say he releases her with a גט, or that she needs a גט and חליצה. That shows the woman in the ברייתא does not yet have a גט, which seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she says 'I had relations' and he says 'I did not,' he releases her with a גט. If he says 'I had relations' and she says 'I did not,' even if he retracts and says 'I did not,' she needs a גט and חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with cases where the two of them disagree. It rules that a גט must be given, and that line carries the challenge to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she admits it happened, she is treated as his wife and needs a גט. When he claimed it happened and then took it back, both a גט and חליצה are needed to cover both possibilities. In both cases a גט still has to be given, so the whole ברייתא seems to be about a woman with no גט yet. That clashes with רב's claim that she already holds one.

keyTerms.meaning: he releases her with a bill of divorce
that he went back on (retracted) his words
both a divorce and חליצה

steps.whatToRemember: רב says the משנה is about a woman who already has a גט, which is why the court forces חליצה rather than ייבום. The ברייתא rules that a גט must still be given, which suggests she has none yet. That is the challenge to רב.

phrases.english: If she says 'I had relations with him,'
and he says 'I did not have relations with her' —
he must release her with a גט.
If he says 'I had relations with her,'
and she says 'I did not have relations with him' —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָזַר וְאָמַר ״לֹא בָּעַלְתִּי״,
phrases.english: even though he went back and said 'I did not have relations with her,'
she needs a גט and חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִיא אוֹמֶרֶת נִבְעַלְתִּי וְהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא בָּעַלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 4 and supplies the point that challenges רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that the woman already holds a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a גט to be given, so it is dealing with a woman who has none yet, and it still rules that the court forces חליצה.

steps.title: רבי אמי: She needs חליצה along with the גט she already has
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rereads the ברייתא so that the woman already received a גט and now needs only חליצה together with it. That matches רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: She needs חליצה together with her גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question against רב. He says the ברייתא never meant she still needs a new גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 5 assumed the ברייתא's woman has no גט yet. רבי אמי reads it as 'חליצה added to the גט she already holds.' So the ברייתא is also talking about a woman who already has a גט, exactly like רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: she needs / she requires
together with her גט (the one she already has)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
She needs חליצה together with her גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'גט and חליצה' means she still has no גט, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means חליצה along with the גט she already has, so it agrees with רב.

steps.title: רב אשי: Two different kinds of גט
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says רב's case is a גט for the bond (זיקה), but the ברייתא's case is a גט for an actual marriage (ביאה). That second kind of גט ends a real marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There, it is a גט for his bond. Here, it is a גט for his relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer. He says רב and the ברייתא are simply talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's case, the יבם gave a גט only to cut the bond of זיקה before any ייבום. That blocks ייבום, but she still needs חליצה. In the ברייתא, we presume he did complete the ייבום, so she is his real wife and needs a regular גט. Because of her claim, she also needs חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: there (in רב's explanation of the משנה)
here (in the ברייתא)
the bond that ties a יבמה to the יבם before ייבום or חליצה
marital relations (here, completing the ייבום)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
There, it is a גט for his bond;
here, it is a גט for his relations with her.
phrases.notes: This means a גט that ends a real marriage made through ייבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — גֵּט לְזִיקָּתוֹ, הָכָא — גֵּט לְבִיאָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same challenge that Step 6 answered
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא of two different kinds of גט)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רב are talking about the same kind of גט, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means a גט for the זיקה, while the ברייתא means a גט for a completed ייבום. There is no clash.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to save רב. רבי אמי says the ברייתא's woman already has her גט and only needs חליצה with it. רב אשי says the ברייתא is about a different kind of גט, one that ends a real marriage.

steps.title: A real case before רבא: he rules חליצה alone
steps.stepSummary: A יבם and יבמה both admit the ייבום never happened. רבא tells the court to arrange חליצה for her and set her free.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain couple who both admitted it came before רבא. רבא said to them: Arrange חליצה for her and settle her case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of a real case. It sets up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sides agree that nothing happened, so it is not only her word against his. רבא rules that חליצה by itself is enough to release her, with no גט needed.

keyTerms.meaning: both of them admit
arrange חליצה for her
settle her case (literally, 'loosen her quarrel')

phrases.english: A certain pair who both admitted
phrases.notes: They are a יבם and יבמה who both say the ייבום was never completed.

phrases.english: came before Rava.
Rava said to them:
Arrange חליצה for her,
and settle her dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם מוֹדִים דַּאֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theory to a real case on the same subject
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא rules that חליצה alone releases her.

steps.title: רב שרביא quotes the ברייתא: she needs a גט and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא challenges רבא with the ברייתא, which says she needs both a גט and חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said to רבא: But it was taught in a ברייתא that she needs a גט and חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא challenges רבא's ruling. He quotes the same ברייתא we saw in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said חליצה alone. The ברייתא says a גט and חליצה. So רבא's ruling seems to leave out the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: but it was taught in a ברייתא (opens a challenge)
a גט and חליצה, both together

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said to Rava:
But it was taught: she needs a גט and חליצה!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that חליצה alone is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא clearly requires a גט too, so חליצה alone is not enough.

steps.title: רבא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: if it is taught, then it is taught. He accepts the ברייתא and takes back his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it was taught, it was taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא does not argue back. He agrees that the ברייתא wins and that a גט is needed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had not known this ברייתא. Once he hears it, he accepts it as binding and drops his own ruling. So in practice she needs a גט and חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: if it was taught, it was taught (I accept it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבא pushing the ברייתא away. 'If it was taught, it was taught' means he gives in and follows it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it was taught, it was taught.
phrases.notes: רבא means: if that is in a ברייתא, I take back my ruling and follow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's reply to רב שרביא's challenge
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא stands, and she needs both a גט and חליצה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא first ruled חליצה alone. After hearing the ברייתא, he accepted that a גט and חליצה are both needed.

steps.title: What about her rival wife?
steps.stepSummary: הון the son of רב נחמן asks his father whether the rival wife (צרה) is also affected by this woman's claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: הון the son of רב נחמן asked רב נחמן: What is the law about her rival wife?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. The dead brother had another wife, and we want to know her status now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once ייבום is done with one wife, the rival wife is free. Here the יבמה claims no ייבום happened. If we believe her, maybe the rival wife is still bound and would need חליצה too.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked him
rival wife: another wife of the same dead husband
what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הוּן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: Hon the son of Rav Nachman asked
of Rav Nachman:
What about her rival wife?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ הוּן בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן מִדְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that comes out of the same case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the יבמה's claim that no ייבום happened make the rival wife need חליצה too?

steps.title: רב נחמן: The rival wife is not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that just because we force or ask the יבם to do חליצה, the rival wife should not become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Just because we force or ask for חליצה, should the rival wife become forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question. The rival wife stays free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חליצה we arrange is only an extra step because of this woman's own claim. We still presume the ייבום really happened. Her words can make things stricter for herself, but they cannot make another woman forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: we force (in the first thirty days)
we ask (after thirty days)
should she be forbidden

phrases.english: He said to him:
Just because we force and ask,
phrases.notes: This points back to the two rulings in Step 4: forcing חליצה within thirty days, and asking for it after thirty days.

phrases.english: should the rival wife be forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָנוּ כּוֹפִין וּמְבַקְּשִׁין, תֵּיאָסֵר צָרָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rival wife is not forbidden. The חליצה is only an extra step because of this woman's own claim.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's claim can make things stricter for herself but cannot place a prohibition on someone else.
steps.whatToRemember: The יבמה's claim affects only her. The rival wife stays free.

steps.title: Back to the vow case: the original ruling about three women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to our משנה's case of a woman who vows not to benefit from her יבם. It quotes a משנה from elsewhere: at first, three kinds of women could leave and collect their כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה says: a woman who vows not to benefit from her יבם, etc. We learned in another משנה: At first they used to say that three women are divorced and still collect their כתובה. They are: one who says 'I am impure to you,' one who says 'Heaven is between me and you,' and one who says 'I am withdrawn from the Jews.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic from our משנה and quotes a משנה from נדרים to set up the discussion. This step gives the old ruling. The next step tells us the חכמים changed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the old ruling, each of these three claims was enough to end the marriage, and the wife still collected her כתובה. In all three cases the problem looks like it is not her fault. So she was not treated as someone who gives up her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a משנה in a different place)
The marriage contract money a wife collects when the marriage ends
'I am forbidden to you,' a כהן's wife claiming she was violated
'Heaven is between me and you,' a claim only Heaven can witness
'I am withdrawn from the Jews,' a vow not to be with any Jewish man

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the final law. It is the 'at first' ruling, and the very next lines say the חכמים took it back.

phrases.english: A woman who vows not to benefit, etc.
We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נדרים that the גמרא brings to help with our case.

phrases.english: At first they would say:
Three women leave and take their marriage contract money.
One who says, "I am impure to you,"
phrases.notes: This is a כהן's wife saying she was violated, which forbids her to her husband.

phrases.english: "Heaven is between me and you,"
phrases.notes: She means only Heaven knows the truth: that he can't have normal relations with her.

phrases.english: "I am withdrawn from the Jews."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the רב נחמן and צרה case (steps 11-12) and opens a new topic from the משנה: the woman who vows against benefit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Originally, a woman who made any of these three claims was divorced and still collected her כתובה.

steps.title: The חכמים change their minds, and why
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים took back the old ruling. They worried that a woman who wanted another man would make one of these claims to get out of her marriage with her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They changed their minds and said: so that a woman should not set her eyes on another man and ruin her marriage with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason the חכמים changed the old rule. This step sets up the new rules that come right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the old rule, all three claims were easy to make up and could not be checked. A wife who wanted someone else could just say one of them, leave, and take her כתובה. The חכמים closed that door.

keyTerms.meaning: They went back and said (they changed the ruling)
Sets her eyes on another man
Ruins, spoils (the marriage)

phrases.english: They changed their minds and said,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אִשָּׁה נוֹתֶנֶת עֵינֶיהָ בְּאַחֵר
phrases.english: so that a woman should not set her eyes on another man
and ruin things with her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר, שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אִשָּׁה נוֹתֶנֶת עֵינֶיהָ בְּאַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the old ruling from step 13 and gives the reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The old ruling is withdrawn, to stop a wife from making up a claim so she can leave for another man.

steps.title: The new, stricter rules for each of the three claims
steps.stepSummary: Under the later rule, the טמאה claim needs proof. For 'Heaven is between us,' the court only asks the husband to divorce. For the vow against all Jews, the husband cancels it as far as he is concerned, and the vow stays in force for everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: one who says 'I am impure to you' must bring proof for her words. For 'Heaven is between me and you,' they handle it by asking, not forcing. For 'I am withdrawn from the Jews,' he cancels his part of the vow, she may be with him, and she stays forbidden to all other Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the final, later rule for each of the three claims. These rules make sure a woman cannot easily make up a claim to get out of her marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case gets its own fix. Her word alone is no longer enough for טמאה, so she needs proof. The husband is no longer forced to divorce for 'Heaven,' so he is only asked. For the vow, he cancels only the part that touches him, so the marriage goes on, and she gains nothing by leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: She must bring proof
By way of a request, asking and not forcing
He cancels his part of her vow
She may be with him (have relations with him)

steps.whatToRemember: The later rule: טמאה needs proof, 'Heaven' gets only a request, and the vow is cancelled just for the husband while she stays forbidden to everyone else. None of the three claims lets her leave easily anymore.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's next question. The husband cancels the vow 'I am withdrawn from the Jews' only for himself, so the גמרא asks whether that vow still blocks her from the יבם after the husband dies.

phrases.english: Rather: one who says, "I am impure to you"
must bring proof for her words.
"Heaven is between me and you"
they should handle it by way of a request.
"I am withdrawn from the Jews"
he should cancel his part,
phrases.notes: The husband cancels the vow only as it affects him, so she is allowed to him.

phrases.english: and she may be with him,
and she stays withdrawn from the Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the new rules that come from the change of mind in step 14, one for each case from step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Final rule of the cited משנה: proof is needed for טמאה, only a request for 'Heaven,' and for the vow the husband cancels his part while she stays forbidden to other Jews.

steps.title: Does the vow against all Jews also cover the יבם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a wife's vow 'I am withdrawn from the Jews' applies to her יבם after her husband dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if a wife vowed 'I am withdrawn from the Jews,' what happens with the יבם? When she made the vow, did she think about her husband dying and herself falling to a יבם, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the vow from step 15. The husband cancelled it only for himself, and now he has died. Does the vow block her from the יבם?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on what she had in mind when she vowed. If she was thinking about a possible יבם, the vow covers him too, and he would have to do חליצה. If she never thought about that, the vow was not aimed at him, and יבום can go ahead.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them: the scholars were unsure about something
'I am withdrawn from the Jews': a vow not to benefit from (be with) any Jewish man
She brings it up into her mind, meaning she thinks about it
She 'falls before' a יבם, meaning she becomes tied to him for יבום

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a vow's reach depends on what the person was thinking when she made it.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
"I am withdrawn from the Jews"
what is the law regarding the yavam?
Does she bring up into her mind
that her husband might die
and she will fall before a yavam,
or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the vow case from step 15 and asks how it plays out after the husband dies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman who vows against all Jews was also thinking of a future יבם, so that the vow covers him.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree: is a יבם like a husband?
steps.stepSummary: רב says a יבם is not like a husband, so the vow does not cover him. שמואל says he is like a husband, so it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: a יבם is not like a husband. שמואל says: a יבם is like a husband.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question in step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, she did not have the יבם in mind, so her vow never touched him and he may do יבום. For שמואל, the יבם counts like the husband here, so the vow does apply to him and he must do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's brother, who may marry the widow if the husband died without children
Is not like a husband
He is just like a husband

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. רב says 'not like a husband,' and that means the vow does NOT block יבום. שמואל says 'like a husband,' and that means the vow DOES apply, so he must do חליצה.

phrases.english: Rav says: a yavam is not like a husband,
and Shmuel says:
a yavam is like a husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposing answers to the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: רב says the vow does not cover the יבם; שמואל says it does.

steps.title: אביי begins a proof for רב from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב's view makes more sense, and he starts to prove it from the משנה about a woman who vows against her יבם while her husband is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it makes sense to rule like רב. As we learned in the משנה: if a woman vows, while her husband is alive, not to benefit from her יבם, the court forces him to do חליצה. And if it were true that she has it in her mind...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sides with רב and brings our משנה as support. The amud ends in the middle of his argument, so the proof finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with a woman who vowed against her יבם while her husband was still alive, and it rules that the court forces חליצה. אביי is about to show that this ruling only fits if women do not usually think ahead about יבום. That would match רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason to follow רב
As we learned in a משנה
During her husband's lifetime
The court forces him to do חליצה
